paragraphs: R' Pargori of Caesarea. He cited R’ Elazar bar R’ Yishmael [the Yerushalmi reads “R’ Liezer of the school of R’ Yishmael”]; Terumot 11:2, see there. R' Perida. Four hundred years were added to his life because he repeated for his pupil, who had forgotten a teaching, another four hundred times. A heavenly voice issued: ‘Either you will live four hundred years [more], or you and your generation will merit the World to Come.’ He chose the World to Come, and they granted him both; Eruvin 54b:20–22 [Heilprin prefixes ק to the folio]. In Megillah 27, end of b, his pupils asked him, ‘Through what did you attain long life?’ He answered, ‘No one preceded me to the study house, nor did I recite a blessing before a priest,’ etc. (But this is difficult: were not four hundred years added because of the pupil? One may answer that before that episode he attained long life because no one preceded him, etc., and because of the pupil they added more.) In Menahot 52b, 53a, he asked R' Ammi. R' Ezra, grandson of R' Avtolas, came to him. Rambam, in his introduction to Eruvin in the Commentary on the Mishnah, says that R' Perida was born before the destruction. Possibly his reading was that Azarya, R' Elazar's father, came before him (see R' Ezra and R' Azarya). His grandfather, R' Hiyya bar Avoy, found Yehoyakim's skull (see above). There is also R' Yosi ben Perida.
